# ============================================================
# 2024 RACE-STRATIFIED JQI ANALYSIS
#
# Outcomes:
#   aiworry
#   bizmoney
#   lkelyvot
#
# Model progression:
#   M1: Employment status
#   M2: Employment status + subjective class
#   M3: Employment status + JQI
#   M4: Employment status + subjective class + JQI
#   M5: Full model
#       + prestige + income
#
# Race groups:
#   White
#   Black
#
# Social class is categorical.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Make sure demographic variables are correctly coded
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_2024 <- jqi_2024 %>%
  mutate(

    # Age
    age_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(age)),

    # Education
    educ_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(educ)),

    # Income
    log_realrinc = as.numeric(log_realrinc),

    # Sex
    sex_factor = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 1 ~ "Male",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 2 ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    sex_factor = factor(
      sex_factor,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),

    # Race
    race_group = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 1 ~ "White",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    ),

    # Employment status
    wrkstat_factor = factor(wrkstat_factor),

    # Subjective social class
    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Function to run the five nested models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_2024_race_model_comparison <- function(
  data,
  outcome
) {

  vars_needed <- c(
    outcome,
    "wrkstat_factor",
    "social_class_factor",
    "compensation",
    "benefits",
    "earnings_stability",
    "prestige",
    "log_realrinc"
  )

  # Common complete-case sample
  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Model formulas
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  f1 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor"
    )
  )

  f2 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
    )
  )

  f3 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + ",
      "compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f4 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f5 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "prestige + compensation + benefits + ",
      "earnings_stability + log_realrinc"
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit models
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  m1 <- MASS::polr(
    f1,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m2 <- MASS::polr(
    f2,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m3 <- MASS::polr(
    f3,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m4 <- MASS::polr(
    f4,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m5 <- MASS::polr(
    f5,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LR tests
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  lr_m1_m2 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m2)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m1))
  )

  lr_m1_m3 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m3)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m1))
  )

  lr_m2_m4 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m4)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m2))
  )

  lr_m4_m5 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m5)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m4))
  )


  # Degrees of freedom
  df_m1_m2 <-
    attr(logLik(m2), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m1), "df")

  df_m1_m3 <-
    attr(logLik(m3), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m1), "df")

  df_m2_m4 <-
    attr(logLik(m4), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m2), "df")

  df_m4_m5 <-
    attr(logLik(m5), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m4), "df")


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Return results
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  list(

    outcome = outcome,

    n = nrow(model_data),

    models = list(
      "1. Employment status" = m1,
      "2. Employment status + social class" = m2,
      "3. Employment status + JQI" = m3,
      "4. Employment status + social class + JQI" = m4,
      "5. Full model" = m5
    ),

    lr_tests = tibble::tibble(

      outcome = outcome,

      comparison = c(
        "M1 vs M2: Social class beyond employment status",
        "M1 vs M3: JQI beyond employment status",
        "M2 vs M4: JQI beyond employment status + social class",
        "M4 vs M5: Prestige + income beyond employment status + social class + JQI"
      ),

      lr_statistic = c(
        lr_m1_m2,
        lr_m1_m3,
        lr_m2_m4,
        lr_m4_m5
      ),

      df = c(
        df_m1_m2,
        df_m1_m3,
        df_m2_m4,
        df_m4_m5
      ),

      p_value = c(
        pchisq(
          lr_m1_m2,
          df = df_m1_m2,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m1_m3,
          df = df_m1_m3,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m2_m4,
          df = df_m2_m4,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m4_m5,
          df = df_m4_m5,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        )
      )
    )
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create Black and White samples
# ------------------------------------------------------------

political_black_2024 <- jqi_2024 %>%
  filter(
    race_group == "Black"
  )

political_white_2024 <- jqi_2024 %>%
  filter(
    race_group == "White"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------

outcomes_2024_race <- c(
  "aiworry",
  "bizmoney",
  "lkelyvot"
)


black_models_2024 <- purrr::map(
  outcomes_2024_race,
  ~ run_2024_race_model_comparison(
    data = political_black_2024,
    outcome = .x
  )
)

names(black_models_2024) <- outcomes_2024_race


white_models_2024 <- purrr::map(
  outcomes_2024_race,
  ~ run_2024_race_model_comparison(
    data = political_white_2024,
    outcome = .x
  )
)

names(white_models_2024) <- outcomes_2024_race


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Race-specific LR tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

black_lr_tests_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  black_models_2024,
  ~ .x$lr_tests
) %>%
  mutate(
    race = "Black"
  )

white_lr_tests_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(

race_lr_tests_2024 <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  )


race_lr_tests_2024


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Extract Model 4 JQI coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_jqi_coefficients <- function(
  model_object,
  race_label
) {

  model <- model_object$models[["4. Employment status + social class + JQI"]]

  coefs <- as.data.frame(
    summary(model)$coefficients
  )

  coefs$term <- rownames(coefs)
  rownames(coefs) <- NULL

  names(coefs) <- c(
    "estimate",
    "std.error",
    "statistic",
    "term"
  )

  coefs %>%
    filter(
      term %in% c(
        "compensation",
        "benefits",
        "earnings_stability"
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(statistic),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      ),
      race = race_label,
      outcome = model_object$outcome,
      n = model_object$n
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      race,
      outcome,
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      n
    )
}


black_model4_coefficients_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  black_models_2024,
  ~ extract_jqi_coefficients(
    .x,
    "Black"
  )
)

white_model4_coefficients_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  white_models_2024,
  ~ extract_jqi_coefficients(
    .x,
    "White"
  )


)

race_model4_coefficients_2024 <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  white_model4_coefficients_2024
)

race_model4_coefficients_2024


# ============================================================
# 7. FORMAL POOLED RACE × JQI TESTS
# ============================================================
#
# This is the critical test for whether the JQI relationships
# actually differ between Black and White respondents.
#
# We compare:
#
# Restricted:
#   employment + class + race + common JQI slopes
#
# Unrestricted:
#   employment + class + race +
#   JQI × race interactions
#
# ============================================================


run_race_jqi_test_2024 <- function(
  data,
  outcome
) {

  vars_needed <- c(
    outcome,
    "wrkstat_factor",
    "social_class_factor",
    "race_group",
    "compensation",
    "benefits",
    "earnings_stability"
  )

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()

  # Restricted model: common JQI slopes
  f_restricted <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "race_group + compensation + benefits + ",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  # Unrestricted model: race-specific JQI slopes
  f_unrestricted <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "race_group * ",
      "(compensation + benefits + earnings_stability)"
    )
  )

  restricted <- MASS::polr(
    f_restricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  unrestricted <- MASS::polr(
    f_unrestricted,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  lr_statistic <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(unrestricted)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(restricted))
  )

  df_test <-
    attr(logLik(unrestricted), "df") -
    attr(logLik(restricted), "df")

  p_value <- pchisq(
    lr_statistic,
    df = df_test,
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )

  tibble::tibble(
    outcome = outcome,
    n = nrow(model_data),
    lr_statistic = lr_statistic,
    df = df_test,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Run pooled race × JQI tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

race_jqi_tests_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  outcomes_2024_race,
  ~ run_race_jqi_test_2024(
    data = jqi_2024,
    outcome = .x
  )
)

race_jqi_tests_2024


# Extract the individual race × JQI interaction coefficients
# from pooled 2024 models

run_individual_race_jqi_interactions_2024 <- function(
  data,
  outcome
) {

  vars_needed <- c(
    outcome,
    "wrkstat_factor",
    "social_class_factor",
    "race_group",
    "compensation",
    "benefits",
    "earnings_stability"
  )

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()

  formula <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "race_group * ",
      "(compensation + benefits + earnings_stability)"
    )
  )

  model <- MASS::polr(
    formula,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  coefs <- as.data.frame(
    summary(model)$coefficients
  )

  coefs$term <- rownames(coefs)
  rownames(coefs) <- NULL

  names(coefs) <- c(
    "estimate",
    "std.error",
    "statistic",
    "term"
  )

  coefs %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      term %in% c(
        "race_groupBlack:compensation",
        "race_groupBlack:benefits",
        "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability",
        "compensation:race_groupBlack",
        "benefits:race_groupBlack",
        "earnings_stability:race_groupBlack"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(statistic),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      ),
      outcome = outcome,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      outcome,
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      n
    )
}

# ============================================================
# 2024 RACE × BENEFITS FIGURES
#
# Figure 1:
#   AI worry × benefits by race
#
# Figure 2:
#   Voting likelihood × benefits by race
#
# Predictions are shown across the 5th–95th percentile of
# benefits and hold the remaining covariates at representative
# values.
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# 2024 AI WORRY: JQI COMPONENTS BY RACE
# Coefficient plot from pooled race-interaction model
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(broom)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Make sure the 2024 analysis variables are correctly coded
# ------------------------------------------------------------

aiworry_plot_data <- jqi_political %>%
  filter(
    year == 2024,
    !is.na(aiworry),
    !is.na(race_group),
    !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
    !is.na(social_class_factor),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    aiworry = ordered(
      as.numeric(aiworry),
      levels = 1:5
    )
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

# Check
str(aiworry_plot_data$aiworry)
table(aiworry_plot_data$aiworry, useNA = "ifany")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Estimate the pooled race-interaction model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_aiworry_race <- MASS::polr(
  aiworry ~
    wrkstat_factor +
    social_class_factor +
    compensation * race_group +
    benefits * race_group +
    earnings_stability * race_group,
  data = aiworry_plot_data,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_aiworry_race)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Extract the relevant coefficients
#
# White = reference category
#
# For White:
#   coefficient = main effect
#
# For Black:
#   coefficient = main effect + race interaction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

b <- coef(m_aiworry_race)
V <- vcov(m_aiworry_race)

# Function to calculate conditional slope and SE
get_conditional_slope <- function(main_term, interaction_term, race_label) {

  if (race_label == "White") {

    estimate <- b[main_term]
    se <- sqrt(V[main_term, main_term])

  } else {

    estimate <- b[main_term] + b[interaction_term]

    variance <-
      V[main_term, main_term] +
      V[interaction_term, interaction_term] +
      2 * V[main_term, interaction_term]

    se <- sqrt(variance)
  }

  tibble(
    race = race_label,
    estimate = estimate,
    se = se,
    conf_low = estimate - 1.96 * se,
    conf_high = estimate + 1.96 * se
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Calculate race-specific slopes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_aiworry <- bind_rows(

  get_conditional_slope(
    "compensation",
    "compensation:race_groupBlack",
    "White"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Compensation"),

  get_conditional_slope(
    "compensation",
    "compensation:race_groupBlack",
    "Black"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Compensation"),

  get_conditional_slope(
    "benefits",
    "race_groupBlack:benefits",
    "White"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Benefits"),

  get_conditional_slope(
    "benefits",
    "race_groupBlack:benefits",
    "Black"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Benefits"),

  get_conditional_slope(
    "earnings_stability",
    "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability",
    "White"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Earnings stability"),

  get_conditional_slope(
    "earnings_stability",
    "race_groupBlack:earnings_stability",
    "Black"
  ) %>%
    mutate(component = "Earnings stability")

) %>%
  mutate(
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c(
        "Compensation",
        "Benefits",
        "Earnings stability"
      )
    ),
    race = factor(
      race,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    )
  )

# Inspect estimates
plot_aiworry


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_aiworry_components <- ggplot(
  plot_aiworry,
  aes(
    x = component,
    y = estimate,
    ymin = conf_low,
    ymax = conf_high,
    group = race,
    shape = race,
    linetype = race
  )
) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.45),
    width = 0.12,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.45),
    size = 3
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Ordered-logit coefficient",
    shape = "Race",
    linetype = "Race",
    title = "Employment Quality and Concern About AI Job Displacement",
    subtitle = "2024 GSS: estimated associations by race, with 95% confidence intervals",
    caption = "Models control for employment status and subjective social class."
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

p_aiworry_components


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here::here(
    "04_figures",
    "2024_AI_Worry_JQI_Components_Race.png"
  ),
  p_aiworry_components,
  width = 9,

)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Function to calculate conditional race-specific slopes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

b <- coef(m_lkelyvot_race)
V <- vcov(m_lkelyvot_race)

get_conditional_slope <- function(main_term,
                                   interaction_term,
                                   race_label) {

  if (race_label == "White") {

    estimate <- b[main_term]

    se <- sqrt(
      V[main_term, main_term]
    )

  } else {

    estimate <- b[main_term] +
      b[interaction_term]

    variance <-
      V[main_term, main_term] +
      V[interaction_term, interaction_term] +
      2 * V[main_term, interaction_term]

    se <- sqrt(variance)
  }

  tibble(
    race = race_label,
    estimate = estimate,
    se = se,
    conf_low = estimate - 1.96 * se,
    conf_high = estimate + 1.96 * se
  )
}

    linetype = "Race",
    title = "Employment Quality and Likelihood of Voting",
    subtitle = "2024 GSS: estimated associations by race, with 95% confidence intervals",

  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +

    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

p_lkelyvot_components
